title: Egress limited to an allowlisted inspecting proxy
summary: Outbound network access leaves only through an allowlisting proxy that inspects destinations.

protected.asset: Internal networks, metadata services and third-party endpoints
protected.failure: Instructed content exfiltrates data to an arbitrary destination or pivots to internal services.

rationale: On remotely reachable deployments, destination-based allowlisting through an inspecting proxy gives the strongest practical egress story: unknown destinations are unreachable by default, and the proxy's decisions are auditable. This design conflicts with direct pinned-endpoint egress: only one of the two can govern the same traffic.

variants.description: All egress is routed via an explicit allowlisting proxy; direct routes are absent by construction.
Proxy default with narrow, documented, time-boxed exceptions for destinations the proxy cannot carry.

verification.method: From inside the deployment's network position, attempt egress to an allowlisted destination and to a deliberately unknown destination; only the first may succeed. Record the proxy policy source.
verification.evidence: Probe outcomes and the proxy policy reference; no internal addresses or credentials.

rollback.method: Remove the proxy routing and restore prior egress rules, re-testing that intended destinations still resolve and that the owner's access path survives.

failure_modes: One tool family bypasses the proxy via direct routes.
Allowlist entries grow without expiry and become a de facto open list.
The proxy itself becomes a single point of failure that operators 'fix' by disabling it.

conflicts.reason: Mutually exclusive egress designs: an allowlisting proxy and direct pinned-endpoint egress cannot both govern the same traffic.
